# Likert (diverging survey)

Contents: [Use cases](#use-cases), [Chart IDs](#chart-ids), [Minimal spec](#minimal-spec), [Data](#data), [Options](#options), [Annotations](#annotations), [Sizing](#sizing), [Fixtures](#fixtures), [Not for](#not-for).

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-reference.mjs from the boardplot describe, list and fixtures payloads. -->

Agreement across statements as a diverging stacked bar centred on the declared neutral midpoint — shares, sign, segment order and net score all derived, and the neutral convention stated rather than assumed. Type `likert`. Aliases: `diverging-stacked`.

## Use cases

- Agreement by statement
- Net sentiment per question
- Employee survey results

## Chart IDs

One form; its chart ID is `likert`.

## Minimal spec

```json
{
  "type": "likert",
  "data": {
    "scale": [
      { "id": "disagree", "label": "Disagree" },
      { "id": "neutral", "label": "Neutral", "role": "neutral" },
      { "id": "agree", "label": "Agree" }
    ],
    "items": [
      { "id": "service", "label": "Helpful service", "values": [10, 20, 70] },
      { "id": "speed", "label": "Fast response", "values": [20, 30, 50] }
    ]
  },
  "options": {
    "values": "counts",
    "unit": "responses",
    "title": "Helpful service receives more agreement than fast response",
    "source": "Illustrative data"
  }
}
```

## Data

| Path | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| scale | array | yes | Response options ordered most-negative to most-positive. Fewer than three is refused AT LAYOUT with likert-scale-too-short, so the author gets the domain reason rather than a schema arity message. |
| scale[].id | string | yes | Response-option identity used by keyed statement values. |
| scale[].label | string |  | Displayed response-option name; defaults to its id. |
| scale[].role | string |  | The midpoint of an ODD scale. Exactly one option carries it, in the middle position; an even scale must not carry it at all. One of `'neutral'`. |
| items | array | yes | Survey statements and their response distributions, displayed in input order unless sorting is requested. |
| items[].id | string | yes | Unique survey-statement identity. |
| items[].label | string |  | Displayed survey statement; defaults to its id. |
| items[].date | string |  | ISO observation date for dated survey-wave comparisons; statement order does not supply a period. |
| items[].values | array | yes | Counts or percentages per DECLARED scale option, positional or keyed. Which of the two is declared by options.values and is never inferred. |
| items[].values[].optionId | string | yes | Declared scale-option id receiving this response value. |
| items[].values[].value | number \| null | yes | Count or percentage according to options.values; null is refused during layout because a missing response category cannot be treated as zero. |
| items[].n | number |  | Responses the row was computed over. Required for percent input to be auditable. |

## Options

| Path | Type | Values | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| values | string | `'counts'`, `'percent'` |  | REQUIRED. A 5-point row of counts 20/20/20/20/20 also sums to 100, so counts-vs-percent cannot be sniffed from the data. |
| neutral | string | `'split'`, `'positive'`, `'negative'`, `'exclude'` | `'split'` | Where the midpoint's share goes. Default 'split' (half each side, the published convention for diverging Likert charts); 'exclude' drops it and warns that the bars no longer sum to the base. |
| summary | string | `'net'`, `'none'` | `'net'` | Net column (% agree − % disagree). Default 'net'; refused with neutral 'positive'/'negative', where the signed stack sum is not the net score. |
| sortBy | string | `'sheet'`, `'net'` | `'sheet'` | Statement order. Default 'sheet'; 'net' sorts descending with ties broken by input order. |
| methodNote | boolean |  |  | Default false. true adds the method footnotes: the forced-choice centre line, the definition of the net column and the sort order. The neutral treatment and the base of the shares are required for interpretation and print regardless, unless requiredNotes turns them off. |
| requiredNotes | object |  |  | The two notes a reader needs to read the shares print by default. Turn one off only when the exhibit's own text already says it. |
| requiredNotes.neutral | boolean |  |  | Default true. false drops the note on the neutral treatment; set it when the title or subtitle already states it ('Neutral split across the centre line'). |
| requiredNotes.base | boolean |  |  | Default true. false drops the note on the base of the shares; set it when the source or a footnote already states it ('n = 882 per statement'). |

Plus the [shared options](options.md). This type does not accept `detailFields`, `categoryLabels`, `valueAxis`, `categoryAxis`, `secondaryAxis`, `sort`, `topN`, `hatchStrength`, `colorblindSafe`, `rounding`.

## Annotations

An annotation anchor is a category or item id string, or an object with categoryId plus optional seriesId, segmentId and edge (start, end, total); pointId addresses a scatter point. Category anchors, including from/to, take category ids, not category labels.

| Kind | Purpose | Required | Anchors | Optional fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cagr | Draws a growth arrow between two anchored points and computes the compound annual growth rate from their values and ISO-date span. |  | from: AnchorRef (optional); to: AnchorRef (optional) | suffix: string, default 'p.a.'. Text after the rate. period: boolean. Print the period before the rate from the anchors' category labels, '2014–2019: +5.8% p.a.'. Default true when the chart carries two or more CAGRs, so nested brackets are told apart by their text, false otherwise. | Omitted endpoints span the first to the last category, or the first to the last total on a waterfall. Resolved endpoints need a positive date interval from ISO dates or year-bearing labels and a positive start value; an end of zero reads -100%, and a start at or below zero or a negative end omits the rate and warns cagr-undefined. On a continuous time axis the years are the exact span between the two readings. An anchor on one series of several (seriesId, or a line category, which reads the first drawn series) names that series in the label, "Product B +10.1% p.a.", and the arm runs from that series' segment or point. In text, ${value} prints the rate with its suffix, so "CAGR 2014–2019: ${value}" keeps the computed number. |
| diff | Draws a level-difference arrow between two anchors and computes either percent change or their signed value difference. | from, to | from: AnchorRef; to: AnchorRef | mode: relative \| absolute \| reversed, default relative. relative prints the percent change from 'from' to 'to', reversed the change from 'to' to 'from', absolute the value difference. | Mode defaults to relative. Relative and reversed changes need a nonzero base; negative bases use its absolute magnitude and emit a warning. Absolute mode reports the raw value difference. A hidden label removes its arm. |
| delta | Computes the signed difference between an anchored value and another anchor or literal, then places a collision-managed label at the first anchor. | at, vs | at: AnchorRef; vs: AnchorRef \| number |  |  |
| note | Places authored text at an anchored data element through collision avoidance, with an optional icon or status chip. | at, text | at: AnchorRef |  |  |
| callout | Places authored free text at an anchored data element, routing a leader when displaced and honoring the preferred side. | at, text | at: AnchorRef | preferSide: left \| right \| above \| below. Side the solver tries first; the label keeps a leader when it moves. headline: string. A bold first line over the text, which then prints in plain type; ${value} in it prints the anchored value from the data. Example: "headline": "${value}", "text": "Peak in handheld-loom demand" prints 153 in bold over the words. arrow: boolean, default false. A thin arrow from the text to the anchored point; the first line sits level with the point, right or left of it, where there is room. Not with icon or status. Example: "arrow": true. |  |

## Sizing

Floor 280 × 28 px; fit `content`.

Below the floor a render is refused with `size-below-floor` and the pixels it needs. `measure` returns the natural and comfortable size for a given spec; see [Sizing in the manual](../manual.md#sizing).

## Not for

Unordered response categories; likert centres an ordered scale on its neutral point.
